- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.6) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to bullish sentiment.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., <0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — add 3–5% to prevent premature sell-off.  
- If recent price history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days trending down from peak), model should not continue trend — adjust forecast to align with recent mean.  
- After a sharp spike (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days), forecast should not continue upward — cap next 3–5 days’ rise at 1–2% above peak to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +/–0.3+), model should smooth forecast curve — avoid sharp directional shifts unless sentiment confirms trend.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent average — avoid long-term drift.
